system.summary: French: letters by number (a 14 ... z 37) and by a second set of signs, syllables in rows of five on consecutive numbers (b 170-174 ... v 380-384), and code numbers for names, titles and frequent words.
system.sibling_key: The Paulmyer letters of 1664 (TKUA Frankrig, unit 261294) use the same code; read here with the Petkum key unchanged.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = rows of key.tsv (155), not signs seen in the text. nomenclator.entries not counted (0 is a placeholder); unread_groups = code numbers met with no value in the Petkum letters (holes.md 2). The transcriptions write a cipher word group with its tokens joined by dots inside <...>; the dots are ours.

prior_solution.where: None found for these letters; priority not established. Checked 12 Nov 2026: Danske Magazin (56 vols, OCR), 155 archive.org volumes, Thyra Sehested Hannibal Sehested I-II, Schoolcraft EHR 1910, DECODE (Petkum 0 records), Cryptiana index, 140 saved texts for dates and phrases. Printed Petkum letters are of 1654, 1663 and 1666-67; printed Paulmyer letters of Sept-Nov 1666. Not reached: Becker, Samlinger (1847-57); Boggild-Andersen, Hannibal Sehested; Danmark-Norges Traktater 6; for Paulmyer DECODE, Cryptiana, Fridericia, Aarsberetninger. The chancery read this code at the time.

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney directed the work and set the rules (transcriptions frozen before decoding, one decode per letter, held-out pages, shuffled controls, every attempt recorded, no claim without its check) and filed the issues; Claude sessions chose the leaves from the repository sweep, read the glosses, built the key, transcribed, decoded, counted and read. No reading by a person without AI.
tools: own Python, standard library: decoder (scripts/decode.py), strict counter (scripts/count.py), blind comparison (scripts/compare_blind.py)
own shuffled-key control, French character 4-gram from four Project Gutenberg texts, 5,000 shuffles, two seeds (scripts/shuffle_control.py)
models: Claude (Anthropic), several sessions of 12 Nov 2026 (model ids not recorded)

solution.what: Key v1 read under the chancery glosses on images 377 and 401 of unit 261267 (Petkum); frozen before any bare page was decoded.
Row rule: syllables in rows of five (a e i o u) on consecutive numbers; fills gaps between glossed values.
30 Nov 1665, pp.2-3 (image 573), transcribed and frozen, decoded once with v1: 162/238 strict.
First shuffled-key control let code-word values count as text: 1/5,000 at or above true. Rejected as a test and replaced by a control on spelled values only: 0/5,000 (two seeds).
17 row-rule values met afterwards under the glosses of image 574 right: 17 agree, 0 contradict. v2 = v1 + 17 values from those glosses, frozen before pp.1 and 4 were transcribed; held out: 50/74.
Code 51 found misread (la France for le Roy de Danemark) after decoding; corrected as KEY_v3; no count changed (code words count E).
Blind second transcription of 30 Nov 1665: 721/726 tokens agree; adjudicated on crops; 220/312 with KEY_v3.
Four more bare Petkum letters decoded once with KEY_v3 unchanged: 218/323; then five more: 103/157 (blind second reader 100/157).
Paulmyer letters (unit 261294): glossed leaves agree with KEY_v3; the bare passage of 25 Apr 1664 decoded once: 21/27. Three sister letters: 73/124, below the filing line.
KEY_v4 built from Paulmyer glosses only, tested on six bare Paulmyer passages: 51/95; not adopted.
Twelve further bare Petkum letters decoded once with KEY_v3: 121/190, below the filing line; not filed, not in this folder.
Prior-art search as in conditions.prior_solution; Becker and Boggild-Andersen not reached.

For this folder every count and control re-run from the folder files; all filed figures reproduce. New: seed 7 for every control; 28 Apr 1665 alone gives 1/5,000 at seed 7 (0/5,000 at the filed seed).

texts.label: Petkum, 30 Nov 1665
texts.summary: Petkum reports from the court at Oxford: with the French ambassadors recalled he holds a [break] between France and England certain; England has no friend but the Bishop of Munster; one defeat could put the malcontents, chiefly the Scots, under arms. He asks to be withdrawn in good time if Denmark binds itself to France to England's harm. Context: the Second Anglo-Dutch War; Denmark between England and the France-Dutch alliance after the Bergen affair (Aug 1665).
texts.note: read_share = 220 of 312 word units (blind R2 adjudicated, KEY_v3; counts.txt A2). As filed in #443 (R1, keys v1/v2): 212 of 312. The reading file was written at the first decode.

texts.label: Petkum, 24 Mar 1665
texts.summary: No need to rush into the English treaty; Denmark's terms will be no worse. England's malcontents have no leader; the [king] is armed and his parliament [sound].
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (40 of 58); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English.

texts.label: Petkum, 23 Nov 1665
texts.summary: Sweden is less devoted to England than the English think. Petkum advises spreading a false [rumour] of a levy of five or six thousand [men] to get better terms ('Mundus vult decipi') and waits to see which side the King takes.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (68 of 96); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English.

texts.label: Petkum, 10 Dec 1665
texts.summary: Petkum is surprised that Frederik III will break with the States General by arresting their ships in Norway, France taking their side and England bare of friends; Sweden is playing for [time] and will pass the treaty of Clifford to the Dutch and the French.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (51 of 75); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English.

texts.label: Petkum, 13 Apr 1666
texts.summary: The Grand Treasurer (Hannibal Sehested) writes that Louis XIV wishes to see Petkum, who has no order to go; he proposes help to a [peace] between [108] and Muscovy to humble Sweden, and suspects Coventry and the Swedes of feeding Juel false reports.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (59 of 94); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English.

texts.label: Petkum, 28 Apr 1665
texts.summary: On the English treaty: if the King resolves to conclude, insert a most-favoured-nation clause; Petkum can put it into the [151] ambassadors' heads to ask for the same two points.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (19 of 26); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English. Blind second reader: see counts.txt D (the share above is the first reader's).

texts.label: Petkum, 23 Jun 1665
texts.summary: The Swedish-English [treaty] has been communicated; Sweden plays the reluctant one, but England would engage with her as far as she wishes; all is negotiated at [134].
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (18 of 29); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English. Blind second reader: see counts.txt D (the share above is the first reader's).

texts.label: Petkum, 17 Sep 1665
texts.summary: The Swedes will do nothing for the English and give fine words only so that they may take [Bremen]; instructions in case the Dutch ships are at [Bergen].
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (16 of 26); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English. Blind second reader: see counts.txt D (the share above is the first reader's).

texts.label: Petkum, 18 Jan 1666
texts.summary: Sweden will not engage further with England; on the 'walk' of Clifford (Talbot) and the recall of both, 'this nation cannot keep from tricks'.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (36 of 50); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English. Blind second reader: see counts.txt D (the share above is the first reader's).

texts.label: Petkum, 6 Apr 1666
texts.summary: To the King: Petkum does not know whether the States General have produced their [346] or whether the French king will [235] the [373], and wants to be sure before taking leave of the King of England.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (14 of 26); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English. Blind second reader: see counts.txt D (the share above is the first reader's).

texts.label: Paulmyer, 25 Apr 1664
texts.summary: The Marquis de Vandy assures Paulmyer that Mademoiselle de Montpensier despairs of the [match] of Savoy because Louis XIV refuses consent. Filed first as 2 May 1664; the passage ends the letter of 25 Apr.
texts.note: read_share = strict S/(S+E+N) per word unit, counts.txt (21 of 27); code words count as not read. The reading file holds the French with holes and the English.

texts.label: Paulmyer, 2 May 1664
texts.summary: Excerpt only: the Chevalier de Terlon is not to act for the French company in Copenhagen; Colbert will use only Courtin, his confidant. Key support only.
texts.note: Below the contributor's 65% filing line (strict 23 of 36); decoded, not read: offered only as evidence that Paulmyer used this key. The reading file holds an excerpt and an English gist, not a full reading.

texts.label: Paulmyer, 16 May 1664
texts.summary: Excerpt only: the French refuse to hand Thudesquin to a foreign jurisdiction. Key support only.
texts.note: Below the contributor's 65% filing line (strict 25 of 44); decoded, not read: offered only as evidence that Paulmyer used this key. The reading file holds an excerpt and an English gist, not a full reading.

texts.label: Paulmyer, 19 Jun 1664
texts.summary: Excerpt only: the Swedes, the Sperling affair, a design to break the Emperor's sister's match with Savoy, an agent at Turin. Key support only.
texts.note: Below the contributor's 65% filing line (strict 25 of 44); decoded, not read: offered only as evidence that Paulmyer used this key. The reading file holds an excerpt and an English gist, not a full reading.
